metric.why: Announced megawatts are the leading indicator for land, power, and equipment demand. The published numbers come almost entirely from commercial research firms; this site links to who publishes them rather than republishing figures it cannot verify.
metric.definition: Capacity in permitting, planned, or under construction per market, the standard unit for comparing data center booms across regions.

reading.body:
Announced construction pipeline, measured in megawatts, is the leading indicator of data center demand for land, power, and equipment.

Pipeline is counted in megawatts rather than in buildings or dollars because megawatts are the unit that land, interconnection, and equipment requirements scale with. The stages included are permitting, planned, and under construction, and the count is kept per market, which puts regions on a single comparable axis. That makes it a measure of intent and preparation, not of operation.

For AI specifically, this is the earliest public signal that a region's compute buildout is moving from proposal toward physical work. Announced capacity has to be resolved into land, grid interconnection, transformers, and generation before any of it serves a training or inference workload, so the pipeline is where the constraint on AI scaling first becomes visible. A market with a large pipeline is a market where power and equipment demand is coming, whether or not the supply exists yet.

What this data does not do is size anything. It carries no megawatt values, no market names, and no dates, so no region can be ranked or compared from it. It also cannot distinguish capacity that will be built from capacity that will be cancelled, and it says nothing about whether the power to serve the pipeline has been secured. The underlying figures come from commercial research firms, and the sourcing is a pointer to those publishers rather than a number restated here.
